South Elizabeth Seychelles Hospital INTERNAL MEDICINE DEPARTMENT Location: 4923 Olivia Parkway Suite 217, Lake Jennabury
PATIENT: Lysander Fairfax Phone: 28451903 email:bradleymorgan@example.org DATE OF BIRTH: 1947-05-12 AGE: 79 years
FOLLOW-UP DATE: 01/14/27 FOLLOWED BY: Dr. Emily Carter
CHIEF COMPLAINT
Follow-up visit for COPD management, evaluation of persistent bilateral lower extremity edema, reassessment of fatigue, and ongoing management of anxiety and depressive symptoms.
HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Mr. Lysander Fairfax presents for his follow-up appointment one month after his last visit. He reports a slight exacerbation in his dyspnea, particularly with exertion, necessitating increased use of his albuterol inhaler to six to seven times daily. He has been consistent with his inhaled corticosteroids but expresses concern over the recent increase in respiratory symptoms. Mr. Fairfax continues to participate in pulmonary rehabilitation, stating that while it has been beneficial, he feels he may require additional adjustments to his treatment regimen.
The bilateral lower extremity edema persists, with Mr. Fairfax reporting no significant changes despite adherence to a low-sodium diet and furosemide therapy at 100 mg daily. The edema remains at 1+ pitting, and he has been diligent with leg elevation, yet he notes no improvement. He denies any new symptoms such as shortness of breath or chest pain associated with the edema.
Mr. Fairfax continues to experience significant fatigue, describing it as debilitating. He has been attending therapy sessions, which he believes have provided some benefit for his mood; however, he still reports episodes of anxiety that interfere with his daily activities. He remains compliant with his sertraline regimen, although he expresses a desire for more substantial improvement in his depressive symptoms.
REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
General - + persistent fatigue, no fevers or chills. Pulmonary - + daytime dyspnea, + nocturnal wheezing, - cough, - sputum production, no hemoptysis. Cardiac - no chest pain or palpitations, + orthopnea. Gastrointestinal - no nausea, vomiting, or diarrhea. Musculoskeletal - + joint pain in knees and hands, no swelling. Neurological - no dizziness or headaches.
PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
1. Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) 2. Hypertension 3. Osteoarthritis 4. Persistent fatigue 5. Anxiety and depression (ongoing management)
PAST SURGICAL HISTORY
1. Right knee arthroscopy in 2018.
FAMILY HISTORY
Father - history of lung cancer. Mother - history of hypertension.
SOCIAL HISTORY
Lives alone in , . Former carpenter, now retired. Quit smoking 15 years ago. Occasional alcohol use. No illicit drug use.
ALLERGIES
No known drug allergies.
MEDICATIONS ON FOLLOW-UP
1. Albuterol inhaler as needed, currently using six to seven times daily. 2. Lisinopril 20 mg daily. 3. Fluticasone/salmeterol 500/50 MDI, 1 puff twice daily. 4. Tiotropium 18 mcg inhaler, 1 puff daily. 5. Acetaminophen 500 mg as needed for pain. 6. Furosemide 100 mg daily (ongoing management). 7. Sertraline 50 mg daily (ongoing management for anxiety and depression).
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Vital Signs: T 98.6F, HR 80, BP 128/78, RR 20, O2 sat 87% on room air
General: Elderly male in no acute distress, appears fatigued but alert. HEENT: No nasal congestion, oropharynx clear. Pulmonary: Diminished breath sounds bilaterally, mild wheezing noted on expiration, no crackles. Cardiac: Regular rate and rhythm, no murmurs. Extremities: 1+ pitting edema in bilateral lower extremities, no erythema or warmth.
LABORATORY DATA
1. CBC: WBC 8.2, Hgb 10.6, Hct 32.0, Plt 215 2. BMP: Na 132, K 4.1, Cl 99, CO2 25, BUN 32, Cr 1.6, Glucose 90 3. BNP: 620 (stable). 4. Thyroid function tests: TSH 3.6 (within normal limits).
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
1. COPD management: Mr. Fairfax's respiratory status has slightly worsened, with increased inhaler use. It is recommended that he continue with pulmonary rehabilitation and strict adherence to inhaled corticosteroids. A referral to a pulmonologist is warranted for further evaluation and potential adjustment of his COPD management plan. 2. Hypertension: Continue lisinopril. Blood pressure remains stable. Follow-up in 1 month. 3. Lower extremity edema: The persistent edema continues to be managed with furosemide. Reinforcement of dietary sodium restrictions is advised, and Mr. Fairfax is encouraged to continue leg elevation. A follow-up with nephrology is recommended to evaluate renal function further due to the increase in creatinine noted in the lab results. 4. Fatigue and psychological well-being: Continue sertraline 50 mg daily. Mr. Fairfax has reported minor improvements in anxiety and depressive symptoms, and ongoing psychological support is encouraged. Monitor CBC and metabolic panel in one month to assess for any changes.
Patient education reiterated regarding recognizing signs of exacerbation, adherence to medication, and lifestyle modifications to effectively manage COPD and edema.
